analysis: The PR changes docs/provider/cli-reference.md only. The visible patch updates the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a documentation paragraph about time comparisons: timeIntervalSince(_:) is used instead of Date >=/<= to avoid weak Foundation imports missing on pre-release macOS 27.2. It also names the build guards scripts/check-date-comparisons.py and scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py. No code, protocol, key custody, attestation, App Attest authorization, cache storage, add-on hold socket, installer path, or fan helper behavior is changed. I found no regression against TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009 through TB-013, or T-041/T-053/T-054, and no new attack surface. The change could only matter if the docs misdescribed a control. It describes availability and build-hygiene behavior (a crash loop) and does not weaken any authorization or expiry decision, and the claimed limits and results are stated as unchanged. I could not verify that the referenced scripts exist or that the code uses timeIntervalSince, because the source is outside the supplied evidence. This is a documentation claim, not a security conclusion, so no deeper review is needed. The remaining content of the two units (the CLI reference around lines 1-792) is unchanged context. The patch hunk lands near head line 1577, beyond the supplied unit range, and was reviewed from the patch excerpt.
